subject: Warm standby RPO negotiation and SLA carveout
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@cloudwave-payments.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Warm standby: RPO/RTO carveout request for EU regions

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the warm-standby behavior looks promising. We ran this past our infra and legal teams and we have one key ask: because our EU primary is bound by a multi-hour replication window to our on-prem archive, we cannot support sub-30m RPO for the warm-standby flow in the short term.

What Cloudwave Payments needs for the initial contract is an explicit SLA carveout for EU failover that acknowledges:
- a target RPO of 4 hours (instead of standard 15m) for the EU warm standby path,
- a target RTO of 60 minutes during a full-region switchover (we understand there's an elevated recovery plan), and
- a documented runbook and notification cadence for activation.

We appreciate Redwood's production focus and want to be explicit about trade-offs. Can you confirm if Redwood can offer a limited SLA amendment (timeboxed for 12 months) for this region and list any operational constraints or compensating controls you require?

I've attached a high-level runbook (cloudwave_runbook_stub.pdf) and looping in legal (legal@cloudwave-payments.com) for contract language.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Director of Infrastructure
Cloudwave Payments

Attachment: cloudwave_runbook_stub.pdf (PDF, 143 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@cloudwave-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Warm standby: RPO/RTO carveout request for EU regions

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear summary and for the runbook. Short answer: yes, we can propose a timeboxed SLA amendment that reflects the 4h RPO and 60m RTO for the EU warm-standby path, with a few caveats and compensating controls. High level items we would need to include in the amendment:

- Scope & trigger: exact conditions that qualify as a region failover (regional provider outage vs customer routing changes).
- Operational windows: warm-standby activation lead time and expected manual vs automated steps.
- Monitoring & notification: what telemetry you’ll surface (primary region health, replication lag metrics) and our notification SLA.
- Compensating controls: longer retention of KV cache artifacts, prefilling critical caches, and synthetic traffic checks during warm-standby testing.
- Pricing delta: a one-time transition fee + increased monthly reserve for standby capacity while the carved RPO is in effect.

Can we schedule a 30–40 minute call tomorrow to go over the runbook and agree the exact trigger language? I’ll bring Marissa for the operation/runbook details.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: proposed guardrails for Cloudwave carveout

Karthik / Mina —

Drafting a short internal note ahead of the call:

1) Proposed amendment (SLA-addendum-v1): timeboxed 12 months, RPO: 4h, RTO: 60m for EU warm-standby.
2) Restrict scope to production workloads identified by Cloudwave (list of service ids in the contract). Non-prod is excluded.
3) Require quarterly warm-standby drills (synthetic failover) with post-mortem and performance baselines — if drills fall below agreed targets twice, Redwood can revert to standard SLA or require phased remediation.
4) Security asks: proof of replication encryption at-rest and in-flight, KMS key management surface. Mina can confirm what evidence is required.
5) Pricing: one-time onboarding $12,000 + monthly reserved capacity surcharge (TBD).

I'll put together a redline for our legal team once we agree the mechanics.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@cloudwave-payments.com>, Cloudwave Payments Legal <legal@cloudwave-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 11:09:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Warm standby: RPO/RTO carveout request for EU regions

Sarah / Legal team —

Following our call this morning (thanks everyone), Redwood can offer the following formal proposal:

Proposal summary (SLA-addendum-v1 attached):
- Scope: EU region warm-standby only; applies to services listed in Appendix A (to be populated).
- RPO: 4 hours; RTO: 60 minutes.
- Duration: 12 months from activation (option to extend by mutual agreement).
- Controls required from Cloudwave: daily replication health export, one 4h window/month where Cloudwave will allow campus-level synthetic traffic for validation, and a primary-region contact list for activation.
- Redwood commitments: weekly replication monitoring, 24/7 on-call during declared incident, and a best-effort prefilling of critical caches within the RTO window.
- Pricing: one-time onboarding $12,000; monthly reserved-capacity surcharge: $3,500.

Next steps:
1) Legal: review SLA-addendum-v1 and provide redlines (we included the runbook references you sent).
2) Security: Mina (cc) will list the evidence needed for KMS/replication encryption.
3) Commercial: DocuSign link provided below for initial sign-off so we can provision warm capacity.

DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/docusign/CW-2389-sla
Attachment: SLA-addendum-v1.pdf (PDF, 78 KB)

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 15:41:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Warm standby: RPO/RTO carveout request for EU regions

Karthik —

Appreciate the thorough proposal. Legal will send high-level redlines today; we also asked Security to confirm the replication telemetry format. Mina, thanks for being available — can you share the minimum evidence list and the expected turnaround for each item?

High level: Cloudwave accepts the timeboxed carveout in principle pending the redlines and the security evidence. We'll route the DocuSign today once legal finishes edits.

Best,
Sarah
